pages.text: "Mumu, why is it dark in the daytime?" Quick-handed monkey Taro tucked himself into a porch corner. Rain whooshed outside, and the sky was dark as night.
"We promised to play here, but I'm scared." Taro curled up, hugging his knees. Sharp-eared deer Mumu sat beside him.
The porch grew darker. Taro covered his eyes with both hands. "The sun is gone. It won't come back." Water streamed from the eaves.
Mumu turned their ears. "Listen. The rain is quieter now." Taro uncovered his eyes and listened.
"The dark doesn't mean the sun is gone. Clouds are passing over it." Mumu pointed beyond the eaves. "Look, the edge of the sky is bright already."
Taro looked up. The sky's edge really was a little white. Mumu sang, "Dark Clouds Will Pass!" Taro repeated it softly.
Farther inside the porch, Mom lit a lamp. "We'll keep this on until the clouds pass." The two friends sat together in its circle of light.
Mom lifted the lamp to shine on a post. The black thing waving there was a banana leaf. "A leaf, not a monster!" Taro giggled.
Taro opened his fingers one at a time. "One, say I'm scared! Two, light a lamp! Three, look for the brightening sky!" Mumu's two ears pointed forward, and their chin dropped down.
The rain stopped, and sunlight slipped onto the porch. Mumu hugged Taro. He was no longer scared of the dark. Taro hopped outside, calling, "Dark Clouds Will Pass!"
